human_tolerance.notes: Judgement: a wary diving duck of wooded lakes, ponds and sheltered coastal water; not described as using gardens or built areas in the consulted sources.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Breeds from late winter to early April; females lay late April to mid-May (ADW). Start date is an approximation of 'late winter'.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Breeds in Alaska and Canada (Wikipedia); same approximate timing as the Canadian breeding phase.

phases.name: absent
phases.note: Derived: US observation curve (fetch_activity, inat-activity-us and gbif-activity-us) is below 0.05 from June to September, while the species breeds in Alaska and Canada (Wikipedia; ADW breeding timing). Monthly observation frequency is a proxy, not proof of absence; October arrivals begin around 0.11 and November is 0.85.

taxonomy.note: GBIF species match: Bucephala albeola (Linnaeus, 1758), ACCEPTED, SPECIES, Anatidae/Anseriformes/Aves/Chordata/Animalia.

external.note: GBIF usageKey 2498329; iNaturalist 6993 via Wikidata P3151 and iNaturalist taxa API (active species).

range.note: Breeds in Alaska and Canada; winters on east and west coasts and inland waters of the United States. Mexico is not listed in the consulted text and is not included.

traits.body_plan.note: Class Aves, phylum Chordata: vertebrate, bird.

traits.limb_count.note: Two walking legs, per the schema convention for birds; wings are not counted.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: Swim and dive for food and fly between waters (Wikipedia: dive almost continuously). ADW: 'seldom walk on land', so Walk is omitted.

traits.flight.note: Powered flight; Wikipedia describes migration and flight between breeding and wintering areas.

traits.metamorphosis.note: Class-level fact: direct development, no metamorphosis.

traits.nest_type.note: Nests in tree cavities, primarily aspens or poplars, mostly in old flicker nests.

traits.size_class.note: Small: 0.397 kg is between 0.05 and 1 kg.

traits.mass_kg.note: EltonTraits BodyMass-Value 397.46 g converted to kg and rounded. Wikidata sex-specific masses 481 g (male) and 367 g (female) are consistent with the species mean.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: Wikipedia: weighs 270–550 g, converted to kg.

traits.length_m.note: Wikipedia: averaging 35.5 cm (14.0 in); converted to metres.

traits.wingspan_m.note: Wikipedia: wingspan 21.6 in (55 cm); converted to metres.

traits.lifespan_y.note: Combined value = unweighted mean of ADW's estimated wild lifespans, 2.5 years (male) and 2.3 years (female) = 2.4 years. Assumes equal numbers of males and females among the animals whose lifespans are averaged. ADW's figures derive from 1969–1973 New York banding and recovery survivorship data with 56–159 birds per sex, and ADW says the accuracy is unknown. The 18.7-year oldest-adult record is not used. NON-COMMERCIAL source (CC BY-NC-SA 3.0), last resort; no permissive source with a typical wild lifespan was found.

traits.diet.note: EltonTraits Diet-Inv 70% (invertebrate), Diet-Vfish 20% (fish), Diet-Seed 10% (seed). The source's Ref_1 is the Handbook of the Birds of the World. Wikipedia lists insects, crustaceans, molluscs, aquatic plants and fish eggs, which these categories cover.

traits.social.note: Judgement: Wikipedia says groups are usually small; ADW says flocks of 5 to 10 and rarely more than 50 outside breeding. Group size 2–10 is a rounded judgement.

traits.activity_pattern.note: ADW: principal daytime activity is foraging (about 60% of time). ADW also says winter birds forage through the night, so Diurnal is the principal pattern, not an absolute one.

traits.defense.note: Judgement: flight and diving escape from threats (Wikipedia describes a sentry watching for predators as others dive).

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: wary of predators and people; no measured flight distance was found.

habitat.use.note: EltonTraits ForStrat-watbelowsurf 100 (foraging below water surface); ADW 'seldom walk on land'. Aerial share is judgement for travel.

habitat.resources.note: Weights taken from the EltonTraits diet shares (invertebrate 0.7, fish 0.2, seed 0.1). Water depth 1.2–4.5 m (Wikipedia) and cavity nesting (Wikipedia) identify the habitat. Water and cavity weights are judgement.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Judgement: sleeps and rests on water.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Judgement: no openly licensed source checked describes tolerance of built areas.

look.note: Judgement: male breeding plumage (dark head and back, white underparts and head patch). Proportions are authored for the simulation model.

behavior.note: Species-local programme fsm-bufflehead-diver-v1: dive forage for invertebrates, fish and seed by swimming; fly between waters; sit on water and rest. Parameter values are judgement.

seasonal.strategy.note: Wikipedia: breeds in Alaska and Canada and migrates in winter to southern North America. Migration strategy.

seasonal.phases.note: Breeding phase: ADW breeding timing (late winter to early April; clutches late April to mid-May), Wikipedia breeding range. Absent phase: derived from the US observation curve June to September (see phase note). Start 03-01 approximates 'late winter'.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Egg, juvenile and adult stages only; no durations used. Wikipedia: incubation averages 30 days, young fledge at 50-55 days.
